title: Aware strikes $226m deal to buy into prestigious Sydney tower
full_text:
The giant Aware Super is backing the recovery of the top end of the office market with its real estate unit inking a deal to take a 50 per cent stake in a tower next to Westfield Sydney for about $226m.
The move on 100 Market Street will expand its Australian office portfolio at a time when major superannuation funds are emerging as drivers of the market, although they are focused on premium towers.
Big funds are betting on a pick-up in Sydney’s office markets, and last year CSC doubled its ownership of Sydney’s Grosvenor Place, moving from 25 per cent to 50 per cent and bringing in GPT as its partner.
Aware Super’s interest in the tower was flagged by The Australian and it is setting up a new partnership with Hong Kong’s Link Asset Management, which will retain a 50 per cent interest in the Market Street building.
The offshore group had bought the 10-storey, A-grade offices from private equity group Blackstone for $683m in 2019, with that pricing showing pre-coronavirus crisis metrics.
Cushman & Wakefield and Knight Frank handled the latest sale, which showed a capitalisation rate of close to 6.5 per cent.
The building is one of Sydney CBD’s premier commercial assets and spans 28,339sq m of office space, with top tenants including the Scentre Group, the Australian Securities & Investments Commission and the Future Fund.
The asset is integrated with Westfield Sydney, is well connected to transport, and sports strong sustainability credentials.
Aware Real Estate, the property operating platform set up by Aware Super, had been looking to add to its directly owned office portfolio and it targets high-quality institutional assets capable of delivering long-term performance.
Aware Real Estate head of investments and capital transactions Pete Carstairs said 100 Market Street was a high-quality CBD office asset that aligned strongly with the group’s long-term investment strategy and commitment to delivering sustainable value for investors.
Citing the tie-up with Link, he said the pair looked forward to “stewarding the future of this asset through a collaborative partnership focused on long-term performance, tenant outcomes and value creation”.
Aware Super head of property Alek Misev said the move reinforced the fund’s conviction in Australia’s premier office market. The real estate unit’s portfolio of high-quality office assets, includes 145 Ann Street in the Brisbane CBD and 207 Pacific Highway in St Leonards. “This was a rare opportunity for the Aware Real Estate platform to acquire a high-quality Sydney CBD office asset with cornerstone government and corporate tenants,” he said. Link chief investment officer John Saunders said the transaction brought together complementary strengths and long-term capital, positioning the asset to deliver enhanced performance on behalf of its investors.
